title: Processing of identified dietary and health data
description: The user manually logs calorie intake, meals, and weight entries which are identified personal data about the user's health and dietary habits. This data is directly associated with the user's identity through their account.
assumptions: The user has an account with the companion app that links their logged data to their identity.

title: Revealing health and lifestyle attributes
description: Weight, meal logs, and calorie intake are revealing attributes that can support identification of the data subject. These attributes provide insights into the user's health status, body composition, and lifestyle patterns.
assumptions: Weight and dietary data are considered revealing personal attributes that can identify or narrow down the identity of the data subject.

title: Collection of sensitive health data beyond functional necessity
description: Weight and detailed meal/calorie data are sensitive health-related data types that may be collected beyond what is strictly required for basic calorie tracking functionality. The granularity of dietary logging may exceed functional needs.
assumptions: The app may collect more detailed health data than necessary for its core functionality of calorie tracking.

title: Potential unnecessary data analysis and enrichment
description: The companion app may process, analyze, or enrich the logged dietary and weight data in ways that go beyond the basic functionality of calorie tracking, such as generating health insights or recommendations.
assumptions: The app may perform additional data processing beyond what is necessary for the stated functionality.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain - depends on actual app functionality and data processing capabilities.

title: Unawareness of data processing scope
description: The user may not be fully aware of how their dietary and weight data is being collected, processed, stored, or potentially shared by the companion app beyond their explicit logging actions.
assumptions: Users may not understand the full extent of data processing that occurs with their logged information.

title: Limited control over data processing preferences
description: The user may have limited ability to set preferences or provide granular consent regarding how their dietary and weight data is processed, stored, or shared by the companion app.
assumptions: The app may not provide sufficient controls for users to customize their data processing preferences.

title: Limited control over data rectification and erasure
description: The user may have limited ability to correct incorrect dietary/weight entries or request deletion of their personal data from the companion app.
assumptions: The app may not provide adequate mechanisms for users to rectify or erase their personal data.

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: The collection and processing of detailed dietary and weight data may exceed what is actually needed for the app's functional goals, potentially violating GDPR data minimization requirements.
assumptions: GDPR applies to this system and the data collected exceeds functional necessity.
uncertainty_note: Depends on actual app functionality and whether data minimization is properly implemented.

title: Potential invalid consent for health data processing
description: The collection and processing of sensitive health data (weight, dietary habits) may not rely on valid, informed consent from the user, particularly if consent is bundled or not specific to health data processing.
assumptions: GDPR applies and health data requires specific consent mechanisms.
uncertainty_note: Depends on actual consent mechanisms implemented in the app.

title: Linking through unique identifier in location history
description: Location history data stored in DS2 likely contains unique identifiers (user IDs, device IDs, session IDs) that can be used to link data records to specific individuals across different sessions and contexts.

title: Quasi-identifier combining location data
description: Location history data contains combinations of attributes (timestamps, locations, movement patterns) that can serve as quasi-identifiers, potentially allowing re-identification of individuals when combined with other data sources.

title: Profiling an individual through location pattern analysis
description: The Health Analytics Service (P3) derives daily routine and movement patterns from location history, which constitutes profiling an individual based on their behavioral data and location patterns.

title: Processing of identified location data
description: The data flow involves processing of identified location history data that can be traced back to specific data subjects through stored identifiers.

title: Processing of identifier data in location history
description: Location history data contains unique references to the identity of data subjects (user identifiers, device identifiers) that are processed by the analytics service.

title: Revealing attributes in location data
description: Location data reveals sensitive attributes about individuals including their home/work locations, daily routines, and movement patterns, which can support identification of data subjects.

title: Sensitive location data type collected
description: Location history is highly sensitive personal data that should only be collected when strictly required. The flow involves querying and processing this sensitive data type.

title: Excessive volume of location data processed
description: The analytics service queries location history 'across sessions', suggesting an excessive amount of personal data is processed beyond what may be functionally needed for routine derivation.

title: Unnecessary treatment and analysis of location data
description: The analytics service performs additional processing (pattern derivation, routine analysis) on location data that may not be strictly necessary for the stated functional goals.

title: Unawareness of location data processing
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their location history is being queried and analyzed across sessions to derive daily routines and movement patterns.

title: Lack of control over location data processing preferences
description: Data subjects may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their location history is processed, analyzed, and what patterns are derived from it.

title: Lack of control for rectification or erasure of location data
description: Data subjects may lack control to rectify incorrect location data or remove location history that is no longer relevant to the analytics service.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Processing location history across multiple sessions may violate the data minimization principle by collecting and processing more personal data than actually needed for the stated functionality.

title: Lawfulness problems with automated decision making
description: Automated derivation of daily routines and movement patterns from location data may constitute automated decision making that requires specific lawful grounds and may involve sensitive personal data.

title: Profiling of individual through health condition inference
description: The app analyzes user data to infer eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals, creating a profile that links data to the individual user.
assumptions: The app has access to sufficient health-related data to make these inferences.

title: Linking through unique user identifier
description: The app uses unique identifiers to link health data to specific users, enabling data association across the system.
assumptions: User identifiers are maintained and used for data linkage.

title: Revealing health attributes disclosed to user
description: The dashboard displays health condition indicators (eating-disorder or diabetes risk) which are revealing attributes that support identification of the data subject's health status.
assumptions: Health indicators are displayed in a way that reveals sensitive information about the user.

title: Processing of identified health data
description: The system processes identified user data to generate and display health trend indicators and risk signals.
assumptions: User data is identified and processed for health analytics.

title: System response reveals health condition
description: The existence and nature of health conditions (eating-disorder or diabetes risk) is revealed through the system's display response to the user.
assumptions: The dashboard display inherently reveals the user's health status.

title: Sensitive health data type collected and displayed
description: Health condition indicators are highly sensitive data types that should only be collected and processed when strictly required for the app's functionality.
assumptions: Health data is more sensitive than typical app data and requires careful handling.

title: Data analysis for condition inference may exceed functional necessity
description: The treatment and analysis of personal data to infer eating-disorder or diabetes risk may not be strictly necessary for the app's core functionality.
assumptions: The inference capabilities may go beyond what is functionally required.
uncertainty_note: Depends on the app's stated functional requirements.

title: User unawareness of health data processing
description: Users may not be fully aware of how their health data is being collected, processed, and used to generate risk indicators.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly explain all data processing activities.
uncertainty_note: Depends on the quality of privacy communications.

title: Lack of user control over health data processing preferences
description: Users may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their health data is processed for condition inference.
assumptions: Consent mechanisms may not adequately cover health data processing.
uncertainty_note: Depends on the app's consent and preference management features.

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Processing health data for condition inference may involve collecting and processing more personal data than actually needed for the app's functionality.
assumptions: Health data processing may exceed functional requirements.
uncertainty_note: Depends on the app's documented functional requirements and data minimization practices.

title: Automated decision-making on sensitive health data
description: The app uses automated processing to infer health conditions (eating-disorder or diabetes risk), which may constitute automated decision-making on sensitive personal data.
assumptions: Health condition inference is performed through automated algorithms without adequate safeguards.
uncertainty_note: Depends on the specific implementation and whether users have meaningful opt-out options.
